page: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 48 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 384.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The CPU configuration provides 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 (including VNNI), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets.

The instance includes 3865 GB of local SSD temporary storage directly attached, alongside Premium Storage compatibility for network volumes. No discrete graphics hardware is present. In benchmark testing, the high thread density yields top-tier multi-core throughput, including 93,241.53 in stress-ng multi-core and 17,654.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 5,034.94 GB/sec for cached 16 KB read blocks and 324.54 GB/sec for 256 MB uncached reads. Single-core processing metrics, such as a 1,703.0 Geekbench single-core score and 28.2 GB/sec single-threaded gzip compression, place in the middle 50% band.

Hardware-level tradeoffs focus on parallelism over peak per-thread speed. While multi-threaded compiler workloads (54,187.0 on Clang) and high-concurrency systems (86.05 million Redis SET operations per second and 64.48 GB/sec static web throughput) perform in the upper quartile, token generation on large 70B language models drops into the bottom 25% due to the lack of dedicated accelerator hardware. From a resource-density perspective, bundling substantial local solid-state capacity with 96 threads eliminates secondary storage overhead for scratch-heavy operations.

The D96ds_v5 is suitable for enterprise relational databases, large in-memory caches, continuous integration compile clusters, extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines, and high-concurrency web application serving.
description: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. It provides 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores, 384.0 GB of system memory, and 3865 GB of bundled local SSD storage without discrete GPU acceleration. The instance maintains a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside a 260 MB L3 cache and AVX-512 vector support. Benchmark evaluations reveal upper-quartile multi-core compute, high memory bandwidth, and high-throughput Redis operations, balanced against median single-thread execution rates. Large-model LLM generation shows CPU-bound constraints typical of non-accelerated architectures. With significant integrated local NVMe-class solid-state capacity, the D96ds_v5 delivers high resource density for multi-threaded enterprise workloads, relational database platforms, in-memory caching tiers, large-scale software build environments, and concurrent web traffic serving.
